comments.author: @lifeonearth68
comments.text: The part about the village stopping for evening prayers really caught my attention. Imagine everyone taking a little break from their day at the same time. Does that still happen in most villages in American Samoa?

replies.author: @MindfulTravelUS
replies.text: Yes, this practice of evening prayer and a curfew, often marked by the ringing of a bell or conch shell, remains a deeply respected cultural and religious tradition throughout many villages in American Samoa.
